domain: Historic towns and ryokan-like stays: Gyeongju (main), Andong, Jeonju; plus temple stays
research_note: Session web-search quota ran out partway through (shared 200-call cap) and many booking sites returned 403. Items verified against 2025-2026 web sources are marked confidence high/medium with URLs. Items marked low are from prior knowledge (pre-2026) and should be re-checked before booking. Exchange rate assumption for USD conversions: ~1,400 KRW = US$1.

places.name: Bulguksa Temple
places.summary: UNESCO-listed 8th-century Silla temple with stone stairway-bridges (Cheongungyo/Baegungyo) and the Dabotap and Seokgatap pagodas. Korea's most famous temple.
places.why: The Kamakura analog: a grand historic temple on wooded hills, best early morning before tour buses. Pairs with Seokguram like Kamakura's Hase-dera + Daibutsu.
places.autumn_note: Maples around the entrance pond and Cheongungyo turn red. trip.com Korea's 2026 forecast puts Bulguksa/Seokguram peak at Oct 22-29 (+/- 3-10 days); weatheri.co.kr (Sep 4 2026) says 2026 foliage runs later than normal, so expect early-to-partial color on Oct 18-24 rather than full peak.
places.cost_note: Free since May 2023 (cultural-heritage admission abolished). Parking fee charged for cars.
places.tips: Arrive at opening on a weekday; weekend afternoons in late October are packed with school and tour groups. City bus 10/11 (or 700 from Gyeongju Station) reaches the Bulguksa stop; taxi from downtown ~15,000-18,000 KRW. Free English guided tours are offered at the info center at set times (check on arrival).

places.name: Seokguram Grotto
places.summary: UNESCO-listed artificial granite grotto (8th c.) holding a seated Buddha facing the East Sea; viewed through glass. Short forest walk (~600 m) from the parking lot.
places.why: Kamakura Daibutsu analog, but intimate and mountaintop; the ridge walk has East Sea views.
places.autumn_note: Tohamsan ridge colors before the valley; 2026 forecasts suggest late October color here.
places.time_needed: 1-1.5 h (plus 20 min bus each way); or 1 h hike from Bulguksa via the Tohamsan trail (~3.2 km, uphill)
places.cost_note: Free since May 2023. Bus 12 Bulguksa <-> Seokguram 1,500 KRW (cash/card), ~20 min, about hourly.
places.tips: Photography inside is prohibited. Check bus 12 departure board at Bulguksa parking lot; if you just miss it, taxis wait at Bulguksa (~10,000 KRW). Hiking up the old trail is a nice nature leg in autumn.

places.name: Daereungwon Tomb Complex & Cheonmachong
places.summary: Park of 23 grassy Silla royal burial mounds; Cheonmachong is the one you can enter (excavated tomb with the Heavenly Horse painting replica and gold crown replicas).
places.why: Uniquely Gyeongju: walking among giant green tumuli is the signature image of the city; next to Hwangridan-gil (the 'Komachi-dori' of Gyeongju).
places.autumn_note: Mounds turn golden-brown; the lone magnolia/photo spot between tombs is famous. Evening lighting.
places.hours: 09:00-22:00, last entry 21:30 (per Wikivoyage; extended hours since 2023)
places.cost_note: Adult 3,000 KRW (Wikivoyage, 2025-era). Some reports say parts of the complex have become free; verify at gate.
places.tips: Combine at dusk with Cheomseongdae and Donggung/Wolji (all within 1.5 km).

places.name: Cheomseongdae Observatory & flower fields
places.summary: 7th-century stone astronomical observatory, oldest surviving in East Asia, set in open fields planted seasonally.
places.why: Short, iconic stop on the walking/biking loop between the tombs, Gyerim and Wolji Pond.
places.autumn_note: Pink muhly (핑크뮬리) field and cosmos east of the observatory; pink muhly is typically best late Sep to mid-Oct, so by Oct 18-20 it will be past peak but still pinkish-brown. Silver grass and cosmos fill in.
places.hours: Grounds open 24 h; lit after sunset
places.tips: Go at golden hour then walk 10 min to Donggung & Wolji for lights.

places.name: Donggung Palace & Wolji Pond
places.summary: Reconstructed pavilions of a Silla crown-prince palace beside an ornamental pond; Gyeongju's signature night view with mirror reflections.
places.why: The night-lit, reflective-water moment; a calmer counterpoint to Shibuya neon.
places.autumn_note: Trees around the pond turn in late Oct-early Nov; reflections best on still evenings.
places.booking: None; expect a ticket queue 18:00-19:30 on weekends
places.tips: Arrive 30-40 min before sunset (~17:45 in late Oct) to see dusk and lights. Flat, accessible path.

places.name: Woljeonggyo Bridge & Gyochon Traditional Village
places.area: Gyeongju downtown - Gyo-dong, by Namcheon stream
places.summary: Reconstructed covered Silla bridge (lit at night) next to the hanok village of the wealthy Gyeongju Choi family, with the old Confucian school (Hyanggyo) and Gyochon gimbap shops.
places.why: Lantern-lit wooden bridge reflected in the stream, close to a ryokan-street mood; ideal for an evening stroll after dinner at Yoseokgung.
places.autumn_note: Silla Culture Festival 2026 used Woljeonggyo as a stage on Oct 9-11 (before your visit).
places.hours: Bridge open roughly 09:00-22:00 with night lighting; village always accessible (shops ~10:00-18:00); Choi family house typically closed Mondays
places.tips: Cross the stepping stones (징검다리) just downstream for the classic photo. Walk Gyerim forest on the way from Cheomseongdae.

places.name: Gyerim Forest
places.area: Gyeongju downtown, between Cheomseongdae and Gyochon
places.summary: Ancient grove of zelkova and willow trees tied to the founding myth of the Gyeongju Kim clan.
places.why: Short shaded walk connecting the night-view sites.
places.autumn_note: Old zelkovas turn yellow-orange late Oct-early Nov; lit at night.
places.tips: Part of the 2 km Cheomseongdae -> Gyerim -> Woljeonggyo -> Wolji evening loop.

places.name: Hwangridan-gil
places.summary: Hanok-lined street of cafes, bakeries, photo studios, small bars and shops along the west side of Daereungwon.
places.why: Closest thing to Kamakura's Komachi-dori: charming low-rise street snacking and browsing.
places.autumn_note: Seasonal menus (chestnut, persimmon); hanbok rentals popular for foliage photos.
places.cost_note: Free to wander; hanbok rental ~15,000-30,000 KRW for 2-4 h (low confidence)
places.tips: Very crowded on weekends; weekday mornings are pleasant. Try Hwangnam-ppang and Gyeongju-ppang red-bean pastries.

places.name: Gyeongju National Museum
places.summary: Best Silla collection in Korea: gold crowns, the Emille Bell (Divine Bell of King Seongdeok), Wolji artifacts.
places.why: Context for everything else in Gyeongju; good rainy-day option. Hosted the Korea-US summit venue during APEC 2025 and a Silla gold crown special exhibit.
places.autumn_note: Garden has ginkgo and maple; check 2026 autumn special exhibition on arrival.
places.hours: 10:00-18:00 typical; extended evening hours on some days (low confidence for 2026)
places.closed: Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok days (open other days)
places.cost_note: Permanent galleries free; special exhibits may charge
places.tips: 5 min walk from Wolji Pond; do museum late afternoon then Wolji at dusk.

places.name: Yangdong Folk Village
places.area: Gyeongju - Gangdong-myeon (~20 km NE of downtown)
places.summary: UNESCO-listed living Joseon clan village (Son and Yi clans) of ~150 hanok and thatched houses on wooded hills; people still live here.
places.why: Quieter and more authentic than Hahoe; strolling lanes and hillside houses echo Kamakura's back streets.
places.autumn_note: Persimmon trees fruiting and rice harvested in late October; very photogenic.
places.tips: City buses 200-208 to Yangdong-maeul stop are infrequent; taxi from downtown ~25,000 KRW. Respect residents' privacy.

places.name: Bomun Lake Resort area
places.area: Gyeongju - Bomun (6 km east of downtown)
places.summary: Lakeside resort zone with a ~8 km walking/cycling loop, hotels, the HICO convention center that hosted APEC 2025, and Gyeongju Expo Park.
places.why: Resort-and-lake evening walk near the hot-spring hotels (Izu-resort mood). Post-APEC, Gyeongbuk is adding night trails, a media wall and Waterwheel Square night lighting in H2 2026.
places.autumn_note: Cherry trees along the loop turn red-orange late Oct. APEC Memorial Festa and the APEC Summit Memorial Hall opening are Oct 30-31 2026, after your trip.
places.cost_note: Free; duck boats and bike rentals extra
places.tips: Bus 10/11 connect downtown and Bomun. Night lighting improving through 2026; exact completion of new night trail not confirmed.

places.name: Golgulsa Temple (Sunmudo)
places.area: Gyeongju - Yangbuk/Munmudaewang-myeon (~35 min east of downtown)
places.summary: Cliffside cave temple with a rock-carved Buddha, home of Sunmudo (Zen martial arts). Daily Sunmudo demonstration and templestay programs (~7,000 foreign participants a year).
places.why: A genuinely Korean temple experience with martial-arts performance; can be combined with Gampo coast and the underwater tomb of King Munmu.
places.autumn_note: Hamwolsan forest color late Oct-early Nov.
places.hours: Temple open daylight hours; Sunmudo demonstration historically daily 15:00 (Mon often off) - re-confirm
places.tips: Bus 100/150 from Gyeongju terminal to Andong-ri stop then 20 min walk; taxi ~30,000 KRW from downtown. Combine with Gameunsa site and Munmu underwater tomb (Bonggil beach).

places.name: Tongiljeon Ginkgo Road
places.summary: About 1 km avenue of ginkgo trees leading to Tongiljeon shrine at the foot of Namsan; Gyeongju's famous yellow-tunnel road.
places.why: Pure autumn foliage spot; easy to add on the way to/from Bulguksa by taxi or bike.
places.autumn_note: Usually peaks late Oct to early Nov; in a late 2026 season it may still be greenish-yellow around Oct 20-24.
places.tips: Nearby Seochulji pond and Namsan trailheads. Go late in the trip for better color.

places.name: Bike / e-bike loop of central Gyeongju
places.area: Gyeongju downtown (rentals near Intercity/Express Bus Terminal and Hwangridan-gil)
places.summary: Flat central heritage zone is ideal by bike: terminals -> Daereungwon -> Cheomseongdae -> Wolji -> Museum -> Gyochon (~6 km).
places.why: Like cycling around Kamakura: covers spread-out sites cheaply.
places.autumn_note: Late-October daytime temps ~15-20C are ideal.
places.cost_note: Regular bike ~7,000-10,000 KRW/day (Wikivoyage); e-bike or e-scooter ~10,000-20,000 KRW per few hours (low confidence)
places.tips: Bomun/Bulguksa are uphill and far; take bus/taxi for those.

places.name: Gyeongju City Tour Bus
places.summary: Guided day and evening bus loops (e.g. Bulguksa-Seokguram day course; night course to Wolji/Woljeonggyo).
places.why: Saves transport hassle for Bulguksa/Seokguram/Golgulsa which are spread out.
places.autumn_note: Night course useful for lit sites.
places.cost_note: Roughly 12,000-20,000 KRW plus admissions (prior-year; unverified for 2026)
places.booking: Online in Korean; English commentary limited
places.tips: For 3 people, a taxi-tour (~4 h ~150,000-200,000 KRW per car) or KakaoT taxis may be as cost-effective.

places.name: Andong Hahoe Folk Village
places.area: Andong - Pungcheon-myeon (~25 km west of downtown)
places.summary: UNESCO-listed Pungsan Ryu clan village in a bend of the Nakdong River; thatched and tiled houses, pine grove Mansongjeong, mask-dance performances.
places.why: Korea's archetypal historic village with river and cliffs; overnighting here (Rakkojae or a minbak) is the most ryokan-like rural stay.
places.autumn_note: Harvest fields, persimmons and riverside foliage. Hahoe Seonyu Julbul-nori (rope-fire festival) runs on Sat Oct 17 and Sat Oct 24 2026, 18:00-20:00.
places.time_needed: Half day (+ evening if staying for the fire show)
places.cost_note: Adult ~5,000 KRW incl. shuttle from the parking/ticket area (prior-year rate)
places.tips: Bus 246 from Andong Station/Bus Terminal (~50 min, ~1,700 KRW, roughly every 1-1.5 h). Free Hahoe Byeolsingut Talnori mask-dance show Tue-Sun 14:00-15:00.

places.name: Buyongdae Cliff
places.area: Andong - across the river from Hahoe
places.summary: 64 m cliff overlooking the whole Hahoe river bend; Okyeonjeongsa and Gyeomamjeongsa pavilions nearby.
places.why: The classic aerial view of Hahoe; also the launch point of the julbul fire ropes.
places.autumn_note: Best at late-afternoon light; colors late Oct.
places.cost_note: Free; reaching it requires a short ferry across the river from Hahoe (seasonal, ~3,000-5,000 KRW, low confidence) or a drive around
places.tips: Ferry operates when river levels allow; otherwise taxi around (~15 min).

places.name: Byeongsanseowon Confucian Academy
places.area: Andong - Pungcheon-myeon, 4 km east of Hahoe by dirt road
places.summary: UNESCO Seowon; its open Mandaeru pavilion frames the river and Byeongsan cliff - one of Korea's most admired wooden architecture views.
places.why: Contemplative wooden-architecture-meets-nature moment akin to Kamakura's Zen temples.
places.autumn_note: Byeongsan cliff foliage and crepe myrtle trees turning.
places.tips: Bus service is rare; taxi from Hahoe (~10 min) or walk the 4-5 km riverside trail (~1.5 h).

places.name: Woryeonggyo Bridge
places.area: Andong - near Andong Folk Museum / Andong Dam
places.summary: Korea's longest wooden footbridge (387 m) over the Nakdong with a pavilion in the middle; illuminated at night.
places.why: Night-lit wooden bridge walk, easy from Gurume Resort; Andong's evening highlight.
places.autumn_note: Riverside trees color late Oct; fountain shows typically run only through October (unconfirmed for 2026).
places.hours: Always open; lights after sunset to ~23:00
places.tips: Eat heotjesabap at Kkachigumeongjip nearby; 10-15 min walk from Gurume Resort; taxi ~10 min from Andong Station.

places.name: Jeonju Hanok Village
places.summary: About 700 hanok in a walkable district with craft workshops, hanok cafes, street food and Jeondong Cathedral.
places.why: Kamakura-like charm streets plus strongest food culture in Korea (bibimbap, makgeolli).
places.autumn_note: Ginkgo on Gyeonggijeon grounds and Hyanggyo (late Oct-early Nov).
places.tips: Very busy on weekends; Jeonju Hyanggyo (향교) ginkgo is the best autumn photo spot. Nambu Market night market Fri-Sat evenings.

places.name: Gyeonggijeon Shrine
places.summary: Shrine holding the portrait of Joseon founder Taejo, with Royal Portrait Museum and bamboo groves.
places.why: Historic heart of the hanok village.
places.autumn_note: Ginkgo and maple inside the walls color late Oct-early Nov.
places.tips: Free English tours are offered several times daily (low confidence).

places.name: Omokdae & Imokdae
places.summary: Hilltop pavilion with the classic rooftop view over the hanok village.
places.why: Short climb for the postcard sunset view.
places.autumn_note: Sunset ~17:50 late Oct.
places.tips: Go just before sunset, then dinner in the village.

lodging.name: Gyeongju Ragung Hotel (Lagung)
lodging.area: Bomun area, 55-12 Expo-ro (beside former Shilla Millennium Park)
lodging.room_for_3: Suites (Numaru-type, Courtyard/Madang-type, Royal) are base 2 / max 4; 3rd adult +30,000 KRW. Each suite has a bedroom plus ondol room, so 3 adults fit in one suite.
lodging.price_note: Allstay (Apr 2025) says suites from the mid-200,000s KRW for 2; plus 30,000 for 3rd adult = ~280,000 weekday. Late-Oct Saturdays and Royal Suite likely 400,000-450,000+. 2026 live rates could not be fetched (Yanolja/Yeogi blocked). Treat as estimate.
lodging.highlights: Closest Izu-ryokan equivalent in Korea: 16 hanok suites, each with a private outdoor hot-spring bath (noncheontang) in its own courtyard, free unlimited use; Royal Suites add indoor spa. Hanok architecture with numaru (raised wooden floor).
lodging.drawbacks: No breakfast included per 2023 review (bring food; isolated); far from downtown night sights (taxi 15-20 min, hard to get late); some reviews note maintenance wear (Booking-style score 8.2/10). Check-in 15:00, check-out 11:00.
lodging.booking: Yanolja (nol.yanolja.com/stay/domestic/3013831), Yeogi (yeogi.com 65486), Trip.com/Agoda; phone +82-54-778-2100. Book now: only 16 rooms and late October is peak.

lodging.name: Hwangnamguan Hanok Village
lodging.room_for_3: Ondol floor rooms and bed rooms; family/ondol rooms take 3-4 with floor bedding
lodging.price_note: Estimate from prior-year listings for a 3-4 person room; 2026 rates not verified (search quota exhausted).
lodging.highlights: Large purpose-built hanok complex walkable to all night-view sites; on-site restaurant; ideal base for evening walks.
lodging.drawbacks: No onsen; thin walls typical of hanok; very busy area on weekends.

lodging.name: Sarangchae Guesthouse
lodging.room_for_3: Small ondol rooms for 3 with floor bedding; shared or private bath depending on room
lodging.price_note: Prior-year estimate for 3; not verified for 2026.
lodging.highlights: Budget traditional courtyard guesthouse, English-friendly owner (historically).

lodging.name: Hilton Gyeongju
lodging.room_for_3: Deluxe twin + extra bed, or family room
lodging.price_note: Estimate for 3 (room + extra bed). Hotel hosted APEC 2025 delegations and was refreshed; 2026 rates unverified.
lodging.highlights: Lake views, indoor pool and sauna, walk to Bomun loop.
lodging.drawbacks: Not an onsen; generic resort feel.

lodging.name: Lahan Select Gyeongju
lodging.room_for_3: Family twin (double + single) or room + extra bed
lodging.price_note: Estimate; late-Oct weekends at upper end. Not verified 2026.
lodging.highlights: Popular lakeside hotel with outdoor heated pool/infinity pool, cherry-tree promenade in front.
lodging.drawbacks: Pool is not a hot spring; busy with families on weekends.

lodging.name: Sono Calm Gyeongju
lodging.room_for_3: Condo-style family rooms (bedroom + ondol, kitchenette) for 4
lodging.highlights: Space for 3 with kitchen; adjacent Sono Calm Aquaworld with spa/sauna.
lodging.drawbacks: Family-resort atmosphere; spa is a water park, not ryokan-style.

lodging.name: The-K Hotel Gyeongju
lodging.room_for_3: Ondol rooms or twin + extra bed
lodging.highlights: Hot-spring sauna/spa on site; value option with Korean-style ondol rooms.

lodging.name: Gurume Resort (Andong hanok resort)
lodging.area: Andong Folk Village area, near Woryeonggyo
lodging.room_for_3: Individual relocated Joseon houses; ondol rooms for 3-4 with floor bedding, some with multiple rooms
lodging.price_note: Prior-year range for a 3-4 person house; 2026 rates not fetched (site unreachable).
lodging.highlights: Hanok houses rescued from Andong Dam flooding, set on a forested hillside; tea, breakfast option; 10-15 min walk to lit Woryeonggyo. The most atmospheric Andong stay.
lodging.drawbacks: Shared/simple bathrooms in some houses; no onsen; outside downtown.
lodging.booking: Official site gurume.kr (unreachable at research time), Yanolja, Naver

lodging.name: Rakkojae Hahoe (Andong)
lodging.room_for_3: Ondol rooms with floor bedding; larger rooms fit 3
lodging.price_note: Prior-year estimate; dinner/breakfast often included in packages. Not verified for 2026.
lodging.highlights: Luxury hanok inn inside the UNESCO village; stay overnight to watch the Saturday julbul fire show and have the village to yourselves at dawn. Most ryokan-like service (meals, tea).
lodging.drawbacks: Expensive; remote (bus 246 or taxi ~30,000 KRW from Andong Station).
lodging.booking: rkj.co.kr (certificate error at research time); email/phone

lodging.name: Jirye Artists' Colony
lodging.area: Imdong-myeon, on Imha Lake (~40 min drive from Andong)
lodging.room_for_3: Ondol rooms in a 17th-c. clan-head house; 3 per room on floor bedding
lodging.highlights: Remote lakeside head-family house, very quiet; traditional meals on request.
lodging.drawbacks: Needs car/taxi; no public transport; limited English.

lodging.name: Hakindang
lodging.room_for_3: Ondol rooms in a 1908 aristocrat's house; some take 3-4
lodging.price_note: Prior-year estimate incl. breakfast; not verified 2026.
lodging.highlights: Historic designated hanok with garden; most refined stay in Jeonju.
lodging.drawbacks: Floor bedding; shared walls; limited rooms.

lodging.name: Lahan Hotel Jeonju
lodging.highlights: Modern hotel with rooftop/hanok-village views; easy fallback if hanok stays are full.

lodging.name: Golgulsa Templestay (Sunmudo)
lodging.room_for_3: Shared ondol dorm/rooms on floor mats, generally gender-separated; a mixed group of 3 friends can ask for one room
lodging.price_note: For 3 people: ~70,000-90,000 KRW per adult per night incl. temple meals (typical 2025 rates for experience/relaxation programs; not verified 2026).
lodging.highlights: Foreigner-friendly since 1992 (~7,000 foreign participants/year); 05:00 Sunmudo practice, meditation, temple meals; programs include Hamwolsan trekking and Gampo seaside meditation.
lodging.drawbacks: Spartan rooms, early wake-up, no alcohol; remote.
lodging.booking: templestay.com (English site eng.templestay.com) or golgulsatemplestay@gmail.com, 054-775-1689. Foreigners can book online.

lodging.name: Bulguksa Templestay
lodging.price_note: ~70,000-100,000 KRW pp/night typical; mainly weekend programs; not verified 2026.
lodging.highlights: See Bulguksa before/after crowds, dawn ceremony.
lodging.drawbacks: Programs mostly Sat-Sun and Korean-language; book early.

lodging.name: Haeinsa Templestay
lodging.area: Gayasan National Park, ~1.5 h from Daegu
lodging.highlights: UNESCO Tripitaka Koreana; Gayasan foliage (Sorigil valley) late Oct-early Nov.
lodging.drawbacks: Out of the way between Gyeongju and Jeonju.

lodging.name: Beomeosa Templestay
lodging.highlights: Easiest templestay to reach by transit; good if trip includes Busan.

lodging.name: Naksansa Templestay
lodging.highlights: Seaside cliff temple (Hongnyeonam), sunrise over East Sea; pairs with Seoraksan foliage (peak forecast ~Oct 25 2026 per weatheri).
lodging.drawbacks: Opposite side of the country from Gyeongju/Andong/Jeonju.

food.name: Yoseokgung
food.type: Royal/aristocratic hanjeongsik course in a hanok next to the Choi family house
food.booking: Reserve by phone/Naver; recommended for dinner
food.why: Closest to a ryokan kaiseki dinner: many small seasonal dishes in a hanok, then walk to lit Woljeonggyo.

food.name: Dosol Maeul
food.type: Home-style hanjeongsik in a hanok yard
food.why: Great-value Korean set meal near Daereungwon.

food.name: Gyori Gimbap
food.booking: Walk-in; sells out, often closed Wed (low confidence)

food.name: Hwangnam-ppang (original shop)
food.why: Classic Gyeongju souvenir/snack, like Kamakura's hato sable.

food.name: Andong Jjimdak Alley (Andong Gu-sijang)
food.type: Braised soy-garlic chicken with glass noodles
food.why: Andong's must-eat; one large + one half portion suits 3.

food.name: Kkachigumeongjip
food.type: Heotjesabap (mock ancestral-rite meal) and salted mackerel
food.why: Andong Confucian-culture food before the night bridge walk.

food.name: Gajok Hoegwan
food.area: Jungang-dong (10 min walk from Hanok Village)

food.name: Samcheon-dong Makgeolli Alley
food.type: Makgeolli kettle with ever-growing anju spread
food.why: Izakaya-like evening; each kettle brings more side dishes.

transport.mode: AREX to Seoul Station + KTX; or direct airport limousine bus
transport.duration: KTX route ~3.5 h total; bus ~4.5 h
transport.price_krw_pp: AREX express 11,000 (all-stop ~4,450) + KTX ~49,300; airport bus ~43,900 (2025 rate)
transport.frequency: KTX 1-3/h; airport bus a few per day
transport.booking: KTX: letskorail.com / Korail Talk app (foreign cards OK); bus: at airport counter
transport.notes: No direct KTX from Incheon (discontinued 2018). With 05:15 arrival you can reach Gyeongju by ~10:00.
Singyeongju Station was renamed Gyeongju Station (renaming finalized Dec 2023). It is ~15 km SW of downtown: buses 50/60/61/70/700 (~20-30 min) or taxi ~20,000 KRW.

transport.mode: KTX to Busan Station; or ITX-Maum/Nuriro (Donghae Line) to Bujeon; or intercity bus from Gyeongju terminal
transport.duration: KTX ~30 min; Donghae Line ~1 h; bus ~50-60 min
transport.notes: ITX-Maum service started at Gyeongju Station Dec 18 2023.
Andong Station relocated to Songhyeon-dong next to the bus terminal (Dec 2020).

transport.duration: ~1 h (train); ~1 h 20 incl. bus to downtown
transport.notes: KTX-Eum began stopping at Gyeongju Station Dec 20 2024 after the Jungang Line double-tracking, so Andong <-> Gyeongju is now a 1-hour hop. Direct intercity bus ~1 h 40, once daily per Rome2rio.
Taxi ~30,000 KRW. On julbul fire nights the last return bus may leave before the show ends; arrange taxi.
Express bus from Seoul Express Bus Terminal ~2 h 40, ~13,000-20,000. Jeonju Station is ~15 min by taxi from the Hanok Village.

transport.mode: City bus 10/11 (loop), 700 from Gyeongju Station; bus 12 Bulguksa <-> Seokguram
transport.notes: Taxi downtown -> Bulguksa ~15,000-18,000 KRW per car (split 3 ways often beats buses). Kakao T works with foreign cards.

events.name: Hahoe Seonyu Julbul-nori (rope-fire & fireworks on the Nakdong)
events.dates: 2026 sessions on Oct 3, 10, 17, 24, 31 (all Saturdays) - relevant: Sat Oct 17 and Sat Oct 24
events.booking: Advance reservation on the Gyeongbuk 'Gyeongbuk Bwayaji' (경북봐야지) platform, plus 300 first-come on-site tickets
events.notes: Burning charcoal-pouch ropes strung from Buyongdae cliff, egg-shell lanterns and fireballs dropped from the cliff, boat poetry recitals. Best done by staying overnight in Hahoe (Rakkojae or a minbak). Oct 17 conflicts with arrival day; Oct 24 is the realistic date.

events.name: Hahoe Byeolsingut Talnori regular performance
events.notes: UNESCO-listed mask dance drama; preservation society 054-854-3664.

events.name: Silla Culture Festival (53rd)
events.notes: Missed: listed so the planner doesn't schedule around it.

events.name: Gyeongju APEC Memorial Festa & APEC Summit Memorial Hall opening
events.name_ko: 경주 APEC 메모리얼 페스타 / APEC 정상회의장 기념관
events.notes: Memorial hall (recreated summit room) opens Oct 31, so likely not visitable during Oct 17-25.

events.name: Golgulsa Sunmudo demonstration
events.notes: Call 054-744-1689 to confirm the day you go.

tips: Best Izu-ryokan analog: one night at Ragung (private outdoor hot-spring bath in every hanok suite). Pair with a downtown hanok (Hwangnamguan) night so you can walk the lit sites.
Gyeongju night loop (all walkable, ~2.5 km): Daereungwon -> Cheomseongdae -> Gyerim -> Woljeonggyo/Gyochon -> Donggung & Wolji. Wolji closes entry 21:30.
Bulguksa/Seokguram: go at 09:00 on a weekday (Mon-Thu), not Saturday. Both free.

Andong works as a train-linked add-on: Seoul Cheongnyangni -> Andong (KTX-Eum ~2 h) -> Gyeongju (KTX-Eum ~1 h), or reverse. Saturday Oct 24 julbul fire show in Hahoe is the autumn highlight if the itinerary allows Andong on the final Saturday (but return flight is Sun 21:55 from ICN, ~4 h by train+AREX from Andong).
Use Kakao T for taxis (foreign cards accepted); taxis are cost-effective split three ways for Bulguksa, Golgulsa and Yangdong.
Book Korail tickets in the Korail Talk app or letskorail.com as soon as the window opens (1 month ahead); weekend KTX sells out in October.
Hanok stays typically mean floor bedding (yo) on heated ondol; ask for extra mattresses if needed.
warnings: Session search quota ran out: most lodging prices are estimates from pre-2026 data and must be re-checked on Yanolja/Agoda/Booking before booking. Ragung price is anchored on a Apr-2025 source (mid-200,000s KRW for 2) plus a 30,000 KRW 3rd-adult fee.

2026 foliage runs later than normal (weatheri, Sep 4 2026). Expect only early color in Gyeongju/Andong/Jeonju during Oct 17-25; Tongiljeon ginkgo and Bulguksa maples typically peak early November. Pink muhly at Cheomseongdae will be past peak by Oct 18.
Silla Culture Festival (Oct 9-11) and Andong Mask Dance Festival (Sep 24 - Oct 4) end before arrival; APEC Memorial Festa (Oct 30-31) is after departure.
Ragung is isolated (taxis hard at night) and reportedly no breakfast; plan dinner first or bring food.
Commodore Hotel Gyeongju and Kolon Hotel Gyeongju: operating status unverified (possible closure/rebranding); do not book without checking.
Daereungwon admission may have changed (some reports of free entry); verify at the gate.
